required_source.actual_result_applied: Theorem F Fresnel-Brascamp-Lieb on the explicit diffuse rank-three diagonal-twist family, yielding |phi(t)|<=(4pi)^(3/2)2^(-1/2)|t|^(-3/2) and density <=12*2^(-1/3).

partner.actual_application: For I={U1,U2,V1} in A_m=uu^T-2vv^T+ww^T+m^{-1}I, Delta^2=8(m-2)(m-1)/m^4 and d=1/m, so the partner theorem gives the explicit but nonuniform certificate kappa[m^5/(8(m-2)(m-1))]^(1/5).

new_results.statement: For the strict-N3 target family A_m=uu^T-2vv^T+ww^T+m^{-1}I on three disjoint size-m diffuse banks, every three-original-coordinate/disjoint-bank packet with rank-two cross block has Delta^2 d<=252/m^3. Hence no universal positive lower bound on the newest partner cross-kernel currency can follow from the three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis.
The same family has target eigenvalues 1+1/m,-2+1/m,1+1/m, strict-N3 physical scales O(1/m),O(1/m^2), yet Theorem F gives ||p_Q||inf<=12*2^(-1/3)<9.525 uniformly for all cap-one product laws.

new_correction.summary: Single three-coordinate rank-two cross-kernel determinant currency is not a universally lower-bounded strict-N3 resource; failure can occur in a fully target-valid diffuse rank-three family that is uniformly paid by joint Fresnel-Brascamp-Lieb.

next_step: If every three-coordinate rank-two packet has small Delta^2 d, prove a quantitative exit to a paid diffuse rank-three/diagonal-twist, volume, hub, grouped-square, ridge, exact-null or physical-pair branch before reciprocal tiny-packet payment.
